    Mister Flimmity Dimmity TESTIMONY

    A floom. He belongs, in the loosest possible sense, to Calsco Fritt.

    His collar tag reads:

    Mister Flimmity Dimmity. If lost, return to Calsco Fritt.

    He gets lost. When he does, a seven-foot Katanzarian goes through the undergrowth singing Flimmity Dimmity, where are you, Flimmity Dimmity, I miss you, in a voice one witness described as belonging to somebody who had gargled gravel.

    He is also a judge of character, which is what flooms are. They make up their minds about a person quickly and people on Maspin act on it. Flimmity's opinion of a stranger has changed at least one important decision that this archive knows about, and that stranger has no idea.

    Mr Armstin INTACT

    The neighbour who kept the air on.

    He maintained the gravity spires on his fragment of the Wake colony: the towers that burn Corefuel to hold down an atmosphere and give a lump of rock something like gravity. Without them there is no colony, and he was the man who climbed them.

    A tinkerer by temperament, always halfway through fixing something that was not strictly his problem, and the sort of person who ends up doing a job because he is the only one who understands it.

    The part he needed

    The regulator assembly is the piece that fails. Nobody can make one any more; they come out of salvage and pre-war stock, and a settlement of his class is entitled to them on request, every quarter.

    He requested them. Correctly, on the right form, quarter after quarter, for nineteen consecutive quarters. His handwriting does not change across any of them. The last one is as neat as the first.

    "The spires are down! I've been trying to get the fucking parts"

    Nardow RECOVERED

    A cartel boss with a compound, a private army, and gold on his tusks.

    Bloated and grey, moving on several limbs at once, in the manner of a thing that has not needed to hurry in a long time. He employs Vitula by the crew, on written terms, at rates that are honestly not bad.

    The son

    He has one, and the boy is nothing like him: a crustacean, wine-red shell, crab maw, green eyes with no iris in them, hair like seaweed.

    He is also, at this stage of his life, not there. The young of some lineages in this classification pass through a long period, years and sometimes a decade, in which the body is awake and capable and responsive to stimulus and there is no one home behind it yet. It is not an illness. It is a stage he has not reached the end of.

    Every asset Nardow owns is held in trust in that boy's name. He is building an empire for an heir who cannot perceive him.

    The Nhath leader INFERRED

    The Nhath who signed the contracts. A lineage number in the hundreds, which means eighty and more generations of one family counted in eights and remembered.

    He speaks flawless Galactic Standard, and enjoys the effect that has on people who were not expecting it. Told that his Standard is good, he corrects the compliment.

    "Better than you."

    The chip

    He wears a Guard translator implant at the neck, bought with the credits from a job stealing Corefuel. He does not need it. He wears it partly because it covers a scar that was already there, put in that exact place by a woman who shot him.

    Who paid

    Eleven separate Guard engagements over nineteen years, paid in full, on time, every time, out of a fund identified in the paperwork only by an internal reference nobody has been able to resolve.

    The old Maspin veteran TESTIMONY

    An old Maspin, met in passing, who fought in the war and has been thinking about it ever since.

    "These kids have it easy nowadays." "Maybe not easy. Maybe I'm just bitter. I grew up during the war." "Some days, it feels like nothing's changed. I thought fighting would fix our problems, but here we are. Other times, it feels like everything's changed, and I'm just a fish out of water."

    That is the whole conversation. It is also, as far as this archive can tell, the most complete account anybody has given us of what the war did to the generation that came through it.

    The palace staff TESTIMONY

    The people who keep the Palace of Riflo running, and who open its doors by hand because the doors have always been opened by hand.

    The red-robed pair

    Two figures at the great oak doors, and the thing you notice first is that they are made of smoke rather than wrapped in it. The robe is the outer edge of the person, not a garment over one. They take a leaf each and pull, and the weight of the oak is real enough that it takes a moment.

    The attendant

    An alien in flowing robes who bows without speaking, receives the instruction, and leaves to fetch appetisers. The bow is not deference exactly. It is the practised economy of somebody who has decided that talking is the slower way to do this.

    Pavlock Jattern INTACT

    Castle Team's engineer, and the reason the room is bearable after a bad day.

    A dark brown beard, trimmed to the jaw with real care and kept that way in the field, where nobody else bothers. It frames a grin he uses constantly. Teal visor.

    Put him in royal robes and the costume comes with eyewear best described as a pair of glasses that lost their lenses and turned to face the wrong way. Not ornamental. Just regal enough.

    Marfeld

    He is from a world where the big predators never died out and the seasons swing from killing heat to killing cold in a matter of weeks. At seventeen he was put out into that country with his clothes and nothing else, which is what Marfeld does to its boys. Three paths: Blood, Root, Sky. He walked all three.

    He drew summer. Heat, insects that never let up, and blisters. The first thing he made out there was a knife barely worth the word, a sharpened stick jammed into split wood, and he kept his pockets full of dry kindling like it was money.

    That is where he decided to be an engineer. Building the thing you need out of whatever is lying near you turns out to be a career.

    No man who finishes the trial may speak about it. He never has.

    The beard

    It grew on him out there, and on Marfeld they say hair remembers. You may shape it, trim it, dye it. You do not shave, and shaving means renouncing your family. He spent fourteen months fighting Guard paperwork for the exemption rather than pick up a razor.

    The rest of him

    Business-minded in a way that surprises people. Face-blind. Hopeless with directions. Warmer toward non-humans than anyone else on his team, without making a thing of it.

    His grandfather's question was never what job do you want. It was what kind of person do you want to be, and Pav is the one who says it out loud when somebody needs to hear it.

    Maspin children bounce with excitement when he walks past. He straightens his back and enjoys it enormously.

    He also carries something he has never said aloud, about the man he follows and the man he wishes were standing there instead, and he hates himself for thinking it, and he cannot make it not be true.

    Quinn Domnall INTACT

    An accountant. Not a soldier, and about to be sent somewhere that will not care about the difference.

    Deep lines cut into his face and heavy bags under his eyes, and neither of them arrived in a hurry. He looks tired in a way that has stopped being a state and become a feature.

    The record, in his own words

    Basic at Fort Actom. 704B, Accountant. Advanced training on Maldo. Officer school at Wedear. Led supply routes out to Fawn. He can recite it in about eight seconds and does, whenever somebody implies he has never been anywhere.

    He works in the accounting division on the Mothership, under fluorescent light that hums, retyping twenty years of financial records by hand because the war killed every computer and Guardnet is barely walking. It is enormous, pointless, and never finished.

    Years ago he started putting small deliberate errors into the ledgers. A private rebellion, one number at a time. Nobody has ever noticed, because what the division wanted from twenty years of retyping was the twenty years and not the numbers.

    Older than the men he is about to be standing next to. Precise. Not brave and not a coward. A man who worked out a long time ago that his work does not matter and kept doing it correctly anyway.

    His contract is nearly up.

    And then a file lands on his desk

    A transfer, to a security posting on a frozen moon called Sonaff. He is being sent to guard a hangar.

    Ranzi TESTIMONY

    An officer Pavlock served under, and the reason he does not talk about that deployment.

    What survives of him is one image, and it is Pavlock's: Ranzi pinned behind the shattered trunk of a tree, one of the tall pale ones that grow like palms, the trunk blown open and no longer thick enough to hide a man. Pulse rounds coming in with that high whine they make. Comms jammed. No line of retreat and nowhere on the flank that was not already somebody else's.

    He was shouting when it happened.

    "PAVLOCK! GET THAT"

    The sentence does not finish. Nobody who was there can tell you what the rest of it was, and Pavlock has never guessed out loud.

    Spara Cavaris INTACT

    A decorated Royal Space Force pilot who left the service, married a chemist, and raised two boys on an asteroid.

    Three decorations, each with a citation, and then a discharge at her own request and a life nobody in the Royal systems ever heard about again. She kept her service pistol, which is regular and permitted, and she kept it clean.

    The stories

    She told her younger son about Modanick, where he was born and had never lived. Always warm. Always daytime. Trees taller than houses. She had loved it there as a student and she made it better than it was, because she was describing a green world to a child who lived on a rock, and that is what you do.

    He believed all of it.

    The last thing she did

    She got her pistol and she killed one of them. There were two.

    She fell across a floorboard, which turned out to matter.

    Forty-five, and the oldest pilot on Nova Squadron by more than a decade.

    He is the squadron's centre of gravity: the one who notices when somebody is quiet, who knows which forms exist and what they are actually worth, and who has read the entitlements nobody else has read.     The Trailblazer doctor TESTIMONY

    The surgeon at Base Delta. Wears a smug little smirk almost permanently, gives you the bad news fast and flat, and then softens once it has landed.

    He is the one who explains floomicide to families: very effective, in very short supply, and it costs you your grip on reality for as long as the healing takes.

    Why he believes in shamans

    He will pull down his collar and show you the scar, a large burned circle in the middle of his chest. A kraskor stampede, while they were clearing ground for a helipad. The horn went through his chest and into his heart.

    "My mates told me the shaman ran over, murmured strange words, and somehow stopped me from bleeding out. They say he paused my dying body. Animated my legs just long enough to walk back to the car. Then hooked me up to floomicide. Call it magic or whatever you want. But it saved me."

    A man of medicine who takes the local mysticism entirely seriously, because it restarted him.

    Vance RECOVERED

    A man who will argue with you about what is true, and will not raise his voice while he does it.

    He has a position and it is not a complicated one: that being right is a smaller thing than being honest, and that most people who are pleased with how clever they are have quietly stopped doing the harder of the two. He puts it plainly, without ornament, and he puts it the same way the fourth time as the first.

    Why it lands badly

    Because he is unbothered. The person opposite him gets angrier as it goes and he does not move, and there is nothing more infuriating than a man who is not competing. Called weak for it, he takes that as a description rather than an insult and continues.

    Vando TESTIMONY

    A Trailblazer, and the reason the Yinmelon story gets told at least once a rotation.

    The run works like this. You put in at small settlements nobody surveys twice, and you sell what people at small settlements actually want: rockroot by the sack, glazberries, spice bundles tied with string. All of it real. All of it worth what you charge.

    The fragmentation grenades ride in the Yinmelon sauce cans. Yinmelon sauce is thick, sweet, faintly orange, and sold in a can heavy enough that nobody picks one up expecting it to be light.

    The one time it nearly came apart was a farmer's market on Monver, where a guard who had been standing in the sun for six hours asked for a taste.

    He lost a thumb.

    Vando tells it as a comedy, and it mostly is, and everybody laughs at the same place every time.

    Yakib Yalitio INTACT

    goes by: Yake

    Castle Team's medic, and the only one of them who does arithmetic before agreeing to something.

    Evenly tanned, because he spends his rest days outside while everyone else is in the bar. Sandy brown hair that falls across his forehead the moment the helmet comes off. An easy, unbothered face that has nothing to do with how he actually works, which is fast and cold and very good. Yellow visor.

    Home

    A world he does not talk up much, with one thing on it worth the trip: a starship wreck the size of a city, Maldo era, so thoroughly overgrown that people climb it like a mountain. He climbed it with his father as a boy, in magboots, which were later killed by a lightning storm and never replaced.

    Faith

    He was raised religious in a way that is mostly relaxed and has a few strange corners he does not explain to outsiders. When he filled in the form that asks a recruit what rites they want, the list of eighty-eight faiths did not have his on it, so he wrote it in himself.

    Money

    He sends most of his pay home and has done since the day he signed. He is not shy about why, and he does not dress it up:

    "I've fought next to you on every battle, but I will put my life on the line before my career. If I die, my family gets paid."

    He is not the coward of this group. He is the only one keeping score.

    Places

    The abandoned monastic quarters INTACT

    Nine districts of Shayron that were closed and sealed, and are still standing.

    They emptied slowly, over three centuries, as the faiths that filled them stopped sending anyone. There is no conquest in the story, no plague, no disaster. Enrolment simply falls, year on year, until a house has four people in it, and then one, and then the city writes the closure down.

    Two of the nine were shut with a single occupant left inside, in both cases because that occupant asked to stay.

    The city still maintains the roofs and the drains, inspects every seven years, and finds them empty every time. They are sealed at street level. They are not sealed underneath, because the oldest sewers in the city run beneath all nine and are still in use.

    Three of the libraries were never removed. The transfer papers say the books would be collected when convenient.

    The Abyss TESTIMONY

    The hole in the floor of the Elder Tree.

    It sits at the centre of the chamber, perfectly round, with nothing around it. No rail, no rope, no warning. Everybody who has stood in that room mentions how strange it is to see a drop like that left completely open, and how quickly you stop noticing.

    Nobody has ever described a bottom. No survey has been permitted and none has been requested twice. The Maspin do not treat the depth as an interesting question.

    After an interment, blue vapour comes up out of it, and the tree takes it in.

    The Academy memorial walls INTACT

    Cast brass plates on the approach road to the Academy, running in continuous rows, with every name in applied gold leaf.

    Names go up in order of loss, once a year, in the eleventh month. Each one gets a surname, initials, a service number and a year. No rank, no unit, no place, because at the moment they went up nobody thought any of that would matter as much as the name.

    There are 2,140,880 of them across forty-one walls.

    Every plate is perfectly legible and nobody has ever read them all. Three people from this archive have tried. The furthest anyone got was the eleventh wall.

    The asteroid colony docking pad INTACT

    One landing pad per rock, painted azure, and the only door in or out.

    A ship comes once a week. It brings food, water, plant consumables, school materials and mail, and it takes away certified Corefuel. That is the whole rhythm of life out there: six days of nothing and one day when the world briefly connects to the rest of the galaxy.

    Twice a standard year the orbit puts the fragments somewhere the radio cannot reach for several days. The safety schedule's advice for that period is to work to the published timetable, which is another way of saying wait.

    The Burial Moon chapels INTACT

    Two hundred and fourteen small stone buildings scattered across a moon of grass, about four kilometres apart, so that wherever a plot is there is one within walking distance.

    Each holds forty people. Each is unheated, and belongs to no faith at all: a rail, a table, a cupboard, and nothing else on the walls. That is deliberate. Any rite a person wrote on their enrolment form at seventeen can be performed in one of these rooms without moving a single thing.

    Services are booked through the caretakers. The average attendance is six.

    The Capital District INTACT

    The ceremonial heart of Shayron: the Castle, the processional way, three great squares, and the old mosaic quarters that are still lived in.

    No industry is allowed inside the boundary and none has ever been. There is no exhaust here and no engine noise. The streets are hand-laid stone kept under permanent contract, the planting is jasmine and citrus by schedule, and the light comes in low and gold most of the day.

    Almost nobody who works here lives here. The resident population is small and works in food, hospitality, restoration or the household. On an observance day the district holds two hundred thousand people, and the day after, it goes back to being very quiet.

    The Council Chamber of Riflo TESTIMONY

    Stone floor, woven banners, and bioluminescent vines kept trained along the upper walls, so the whole room has a faint blue underlight before anyone lights anything.

    A ceremonial bowl sits in the centre. When it is lit at the opening of a session, every seated councillor's flame answers it, each one a different colour, and the room reads at a glance as a set of individuals rather than a body.

    The floor hums

    Everyone who has stood in that chamber says so, and none of them says it as a figure of speech. The stone carries the mood of the room. Anger, amusement, doubt, all of it comes up through your feet before anybody speaks.

    Records are taken by hand with feathered quills. Gavels are used. A vote is not counted; the flames change colour, and unanimity is all of them going white at once.

    The Elder Tree TESTIMONY

    One tree, hollow at the base, going up into cloud. Inside it there is a chamber with mosaic walls and a chandelier, and in the middle of the floor there is a hole.

    Inside

    Every account agrees on the room: the mosaic, the light hanging above, humans and Maspin standing together with no arrangement made for either, and the opening at the centre with nothing around it.

    Height

    Nobody has measured it. Every informant describes the crown entering cloud. Trailblazer survey work in the surrounding concession recorded canopy heights across the district and stopped at the edge of the ceremonial ground, by agreement.

    What it is for

    The dead go into the hole. Blue vapour comes back up afterwards and is taken into the tree. The Maspin hold that what goes down returns to the ocean beneath the crust and that the tree drinks from it.

    One thing we can add

    The district around this tree is exceptionally fertile, and nothing is imported into it.

    Attributed to C., Base Delta, and to four Maspin informants who asked to be recorded together.

    The gem mosaic wall TESTIMONY

    The inside of the Elder Tree is covered in coloured stones, and every one of them is a person.

    When a Maspin is interred, the stone is taken off the necklace they wore in life and set into the wall. There are thousands. Nobody has counted them and nobody has been asked to.

    There is no order to it. Not by date, not by family, not by anything. A stone goes wherever there is room. There are no names, no dates, and no inscriptions of any kind, so a family cannot come back and find their own.

    Asked about that, they say it is not what the wall is for.

    The Grand Mothership Dining Hall INTACT

    Warm tans and golds, in a ship that is otherwise white and blue all the way through. It is the only room aboard that does not look like a machine.

    It seats the entire embarked complement in three sittings, and it cost more to fit out than the medical wing, which is in the accounts and has never been commented on.

    You are required to come out of armour to eat. The standing order gives the reason as morale, and it is correct: it is the one hour of the day when a unit stops looking like a unit and starts looking like five people who know each other.

    The High Castle INTACT

    The crown's house on Shayron. Four wings around a court, raised across two centuries in four separate building campaigns, none of which matched the last.

    The bones of it are Maldo steel, shipped in from the old capital while that world still had an industry. The eastern towers are the oldest section standing and carry more of the original metal than anything else in the building.

    That matters more than it sounds. Maldo ore is worked out. There is no more of that steel anywhere, so every repair since has been made in some other alloy that does not quite match, and the maintenance records track the building as a falling percentage of itself.

    The court and the western wing open to the public eleven days a year. The rest is the household's.

    J.LOT INTACT

    A belt formation with nothing in it worth having: no settlement, no licence, nothing to mine.

    What it does have is rock, in quantity, at speed, in a pattern that makes flying through it fast a genuinely stupid idea. The navigational schedules carry a standing advisory against powered transit at speed.

    It appears in the Guard's disciplinary returns eighty-eight times in eleven years, always as the location, always in a charge about unauthorised use of a vessel. Young pilots have been doing this for as long as there have been young pilots.

    Kelton City INTACT

    The only city in the breadbasket, on the only world in it that grows nothing.

    Everything that decides what happens to the food is in here: the exchange, the harvest ledger, the licensing office, the seed registry, the water allocation desk, quarantine, the port, the crop laboratories, forty-one embassies, and every insurer writing agricultural risk in the system.

    It is a city of offices in the middle of a planet of empty ground, and it clears twenty-one billion credits a year without a field anywhere inside the municipal boundary.

    The Mothership INTACT

    The Guard's home. A single hull carrying operations, administration, medicine, courts, workshops and everybody's quarters, permanently on the move.

    It runs a fixed circuit of the member worlds, published a year in advance, and takes rather more than a standard year to get all the way round. That circuit governs everyone's life aboard: when it is in a busy sector you deploy every couple of weeks, and when it is not, you have a month with nothing to do. People plan around it the way other people plan around seasons.

    There are no separate branches. Pilots, infantry, engineers, doctors, clerks and the judge advocate share the same corridors, the same messes and the same seniority list. A commodore and a staff sergeant queue for the same food.

    Somebody described it as being like college, in that you have free time and choose what to do with it, and the timetable is still pointed straight at you.

    The Palace of Riflo TESTIMONY

    The big stone building at the heart of Riflo, holding the Council chamber and the temple attached to it.

    Vines have been growing into the stonework for a very long time and were never cleared, so the building and the jungle have arrived at an arrangement. Visitors consistently describe it as older than the settlement around it. No foundation date exists and no local authority claims to have one.

    The temple is kept by a caretaker staff, some of whom are working off an indenture, which on Maspin is lawful and is administered by the Council that sits upstairs.

    Riflo INTACT

    The main settlement of the settled belt, and as close as Maspin gets to a city.

    It sits where the jungle allows it: low buildings, stone and grown timber, walkways that go around trees rather than through them, and the Palace at the middle of it with the Council inside. Everything on this world that involves a decision happens here.

    The port is the other half of the place. Almost every ship that touches Maspin is a Trailblazer hull or chartered by one, which is a small number of arrivals for a whole world and a very large number for this one. Crews come through, drink the local wine, and leave.

    It is the only place on Maspin where a visitor is unremarkable, and the only place most Maspin will ever see an outsider.

    The Shayron lamp posts INTACT

    Two thousand four hundred and eleven cast standards down the Capital District, brought in from Maldo when Maldo still made things.

    They have been repaired constantly ever since, one broken section at a time, with whatever was to hand. Maldo steel has not been to hand for a very long time.

    Go through the repair books and no standard in the district still holds a majority of its original metal. Not one. The city continues to call them the Maldo standards, and a clerk in the district office wrote in the margin of one return: at what point are these something else.

    The Shayron sewers INTACT

    The oldest thing on Shayron still doing its job.

    They were cut for the first city on this site and they have outlasted three more built on top. Gravity-fed, stone-lined, and never once replaced, because every era that inherited them checked, found them sound, and got on with something else. Sections have been extended. Nothing has been rebuilt.

    Four hundred and eleven kilometres are mapped. The survey notes a further unknown length inherited from the earliest works, unmapped, and in service.

    They run under the sealed quarters, which are locked at street level and open from below. The city knows. It has never been treated as a problem.

    Trailblazer Base Delta INTACT

    A Trailblazer port on Maspin, built up into the trees.

    Bungalows on stilts and platforms, woven rugs, ferns everywhere, lanterns strung between branches, and the Elder Tree going up out of sight beyond the edge of it. There is a medbay with two theatres, a machine shop, and ground for four medium hulls. Flooms are kept in the surrounding district and largely do as they please.

    No walls

    No perimeter, no watchtowers, no emplacements, no guards. This is true of every Trailblazer installation and it is deliberate: they are guests on somebody's world and they build like guests. Soldiers who see it for the first time tend to describe it as a trap someone forgot to set.

    Maspin work here at every grade, including running things, which is not the arrangement anywhere else on this world.

    Wake Extraction Station INTACT

    The works where the homeworld gets turned into fuel. In the paperwork it is called Station, without a qualifier, because there is only one.

    Raw fragment material comes in, synthesis happens, and certified Corefuel goes out to Guard transports. Everything that flies anywhere begins here.

    The quota

    The Board sets a number each year and the station meets it. The contract pays on certification of the full year's quota and not before, which means a station chief spends every year working toward a single date. Miss it and the year pays nothing.

    The final year on record came in at 443.6 tonnes over.

    Class 2

    That rating entitles the station to point-defence parts every quarter, on request. The entitlements are all on file. The delivery notes are kept somewhere else and that series has gaps in it.

    The Wakeful Islands INFERRED

    What people called the rocks they lived on. It is not a filing term. We use it because they use it, and because no document we hold has a name for the inhabited part of a dead planet.

    How many

    Sixty-one fragments are catalogued as worth extracting from. Some unstated number of those carried people. Our estimate of nine to thirty comes from counting gravity spire installations on the parts requisitions, and should be treated as exactly that good.

    Why nobody was counted

    They lived there under an extraction licence, not a settlement charter. In law they were not colonists. There was therefore no settlement roll to be on, which is how a place with a school ends up with no population figure.

    What it was like, from testimony: houses linked by intercom because there was no network to link them with. One landing pad a fragment, one supply run a week. Gardens under spire air. And twice a standard year, for several days, an orbital condition that took the radio out entirely and against which the only remedy was to work to the published timetable.

    The accounting division INTACT

    A very large room full of desks, fluorescent light that hums, and people retyping the past.

    Every financial record the Guard had died in GC 4401 along with every other computer in existence. What survived was paper duplicates, in cabinets, scattered across a hundred worlds. So the division has spent decades typing twenty years of accounts back in by hand.

    Clerical strength went from 411 to over nine thousand during that programme and never came back down.

    Nobody has ever audited the result. There is no body with the standing to do it, and the division audits itself. What the Guard wanted out of twenty years of retyping was the twenty years.

    The Autumnals RECOVERED

    [ENTRY NOT RECOVERED]

    One side of the war that ended the old world, and we cannot tell you a single thing they believed.

    Everyone knows the name. It is spoken on every world we have visited, mostly as an accusation, by people who were not born when the fighting stopped. Say it in a bar on the rim and somebody will tell you they started it and we are the ones cleaning up the mess.

    Nothing they wrote survives

    No charter, no proclamation, no orders, no requisitions, no letters, no ledgers. Not one page produced by that party is held anywhere we have been able to reach. We have appealed publicly three times and received nothing.

    What physically exists, in full

    One hull section, unpowered, in a salvage yard. One banner in a museum on Sansvor, catalogued as captured colours, with no provenance attached. One uniform tunic in a private collection on Maldo. Two sleeves, no insignia, no maker's mark.

    All three are dark, in shades between orange and brown. Nobody can tell us whether that was their colour or whether that is what sixty years does to cloth.

    A name

    They chose it themselves, which is unusual. The other side used an acronym. A civilisation that names itself after the end of a season has already decided something about where it thinks it is.

    C.O.R.D. RECOVERED

    Compact of Realms in Defense · vernacular: the Cord

    Defensive bloc formed by established institutional powers in response to the spread of the Autumnal movement. Belligerent party to the Great War. Dissolved by the destruction of its constituent members.

    Formation

    2 gaps

    The founding instrument survives in two partial copies, both fire-damaged. The recoverable text opens: "The undersigned realms, being severally threatened in their [...] and having no confidence in the sufficiency of separate defence [...]" The list of signatories is legible in nineteen places and illegible in what appears to be a further thirty to forty.

    Structure

    A compact of sovereign parties, not a state. Contributions were assessed against each member's own accounting and collected by the member itself. There is no recovered evidence of a unified command. There is a considerable quantity of recovered correspondence about establishing one.

    The Wipe

    1 gap

    Attributed to C.O.R.D. by the Guard and by general account. The stated reasoning, which appears in Guard educational material and in no C.O.R.D. document we hold, is that the object was to cripple Autumnal coordination. No order authorising the event has been recovered. [NO SURVIVING PRIMARY SOURCE]

    The Restoration observes that the name is an acronym, that the Autumnals named themselves, and that this difference is remarked upon by informants across a dozen unconnected worlds without prompting.

    The cartels CONTESTED

    Not one organisation. Between nineteen and thirty of any size, depending on what you count, operating wherever the Guard's reach runs out.

    Substances, weapons, transit, protection, labour supply, licensing fraud. The usual list, at scale.

    How they took Astonia, which is the case everyone knows because it ended in an annexation and the papers came out. They came in through the nightlife, then the property, then the lending, and then they bought the municipal offices and eventually the territorial government.

    Not one shot was fired at any stage. It was all transactions, which is why there is a paper trail.

    And they behaved themselves at home. Astonia under the cartels was orderly, because Astonia was where the money came from. What the same organisations did elsewhere was not orderly at all.

    The contested part

    Guard material presents the cartels as an outside threat to the member worlds. The prosecution returns show that most of the substances, weapons and transit involved were Guard-made or Guard-licensed at some earlier point, and had left Guard hands somewhere along the way.

    The returns do not record how.

    The Council of Riflo TESTIMONY

    Governing council of the settled belt, Maspin. Composition is by seat rather than by election, and the Restoration has not established how a seat is filled.

    Address

    Councillors are addressed as the Council and by nothing else. They do not give their names to outsiders and they do not appear to use them with each other in session. This is a rule of the body, not a courtesy, and no visitor has ever been given the reason for it.

    Seats

    Nobody outside Maspin knows how many there are or how you get one. Seats are not elected in any sense a visitor would recognise, are not obviously inherited, and are not explained. What is known is that one of them belongs to the Trailblazers, has since GC 4451, and is held by a human, which suggests the body can add a seat when it decides to.

    This is a remote world that has had very few long-term visitors and no interest in being surveyed. Almost everything in this entry comes from people who were guests.

    Proceedings

    Catalogued under the Council Chamber. Decision is expressed through the councillors' flames. Unanimity is described as their merging to a single white.

    Competences, as reported

    Taxation and remittance to the Royal treasury. Land and concession. Labour, including the administration of indenture. Rites and observance. Relief.

    Relief

    The Council's own submissions to the Royal treasury are held here in copy and record fourteen applications for assistance over nineteen years following eruption, quake, flood and crop loss. No reply to any of them is held by this archive, and the Council states that none was received.

    Indenture

    Administered by the Council. The Restoration notes, from the Council's own registers, that indentured persons are in a number of recorded cases assigned to establishments controlled by the family of a sitting councillor. The registers record this openly, there being no provision under which it would need to be concealed.

    The Guard INTACT

    A police force on a small world with a port, which is now the largest thing in the galaxy. It did not fight the war. It was incorporated four years after the war stopped, by people who had.

    Founding

    The incorporation instrument survives and names nine founders by name and prior title. Four were general officers of armies that no longer existed. Five held commercial interests in shipping, insurance and salvage.

    It constitutes the body as a chartered corporation selling security to subscribing worlds. That is what it is. Everything since has been growth.

    The first world is not named in the instrument, and we have not been able to establish it.

    What you get for joining

    Defence, and free movement of persons between every member world.

    Read the accession debates and it is the second one they talk about. We hold eleven in full, and in nine of them the right to go somewhere is the argument that carries the vote. That is what a galaxy remembers after it has watched borders decide who lived.

    What you give

    An assessed share of revenue, and people. Your own laws, religion, holidays and government stay yours. Planetary law can be struck by the Guard at any time and almost never is, because the Guard wants the money and not the argument.

    Not an army, a company

    There are no branches. Flight, ground, engineering, medical and administrative divisions share the same hull, the same mess and the same seniority list. Nobody serves in a national contingent; absorbed formations enter as individuals, which is why no formation in the establishment is older than the Guard itself.

    Not enlistment, contract

    Fixed term, completion bonus per operation. Units bid for the work that is going, and units with strong completion records win what they bid on. Acceptance rates are filed by unit.

    Nobody is assigned. Everybody applies.

    Standing order 41

    Materiel at a cleared objective is recovered rather than destroyed, and a schedule sets out what the recovering personnel may keep. The schedule has been widened twice. Retained items are not entered anywhere, on the stated ground that entering them would be disproportionate.

    Enforcement

    Galactic Standard law is universal and binding. Nothing in it requires enforcement to be even, provides a complaint for uneven enforcement, or names a body to hear one.

    The laws are not there to be applied. They are there to be available.

    The Guard Academy INTACT

    Where the Guard raises the people it will employ.

    Two ways in. The ordinary one is an application at the usual age from a member world. The other is wardship: when an action leaves a child with nobody, and the Guard was there, the Guard takes the child.

    Over the last twenty years that is 41,880 children. The average age when they come in is seven.

    They get a real education, better than most worlds manage, plus service instruction from about twelve and a specialist stream from fifteen. Poetry, mathematics, languages, the lot. Eleven periods across the entire course are spent on the history of the Great War.

    Ordinary entrants join the service at a rate of about six in ten. Wardship entrants join at ninety-four in a hundred, which is not surprising, because the Academy is the only home they have.

    The Guard Board of Directors INTACT

    Seven people run the galaxy. They elected each other, and any of them can be removed by the other six.

    That is the whole constitution and it has never been amended. No member world confirms them. No citizen votes on them. There is no term, no appeal, and nobody outside the room to appeal to.

    What they hold

    The money. Every exclusive licence the Guard owns, including Corefuel. Every senior appointment. Authorisation of any operation above a certain size. Standing orders. And the power to strike any law on any member world.

    Who they are

    People with commercial interests, undeclared, because nothing requires them to declare and nothing requires Guard contracts to be advertised. One seat has always gone to a general, which the founding document does not require and which has happened every time anyway.

    What the minutes look like

    In nineteen years, 1,411 resolutions. 1,388 of them carried without a division, which means nobody asked for a count. There is no way to record a dissent on the form and nobody has ever asked for one to be added.

    Seven people who can each be fired by the other six will agree with each other about almost everything. Not because they are told to. Because none of them wants to be the one who objected.

    The High Council INTACT

    The senior ministers, the service chiefs, and the heads of the great houses, sitting on Maldo. Ordinarily they advise. They do not legislate and they do not command.

    Except

    The High Emergency Council Act says that if the sovereign proclaims an emergency, everything the crown and parliament hold passes to this Council.

    The Act is precise about the proclamation and precise about the transfer. It says nothing about how long it lasts, how it ends, who reviews it, or what would revoke it. Parliament on Maldo has noticed this out loud four times, most recently in GC 4438, and amended it none.

    And the geography

    The Act moves power to a body sitting on Maldo. The sovereign proclaims from Shayron. Those are not in the same system.

    It has never been invoked.

    House Polaris INTACT

    The family that took a star's name, and now owns what grows under it.

    They were working that system a thousand years before they were royal. The oldest instruments are commercial and show a family adopting the name of the sun they happened to be under. They have not held land there in a very long time and they hold the licence on everything the system produces.

    Royalty on the Polaris harvest last year: 411,880,600 credits. That is more than the entire assessed revenue of nine member worlds.

    The bit that bothers people

    The star, the system, the shared calendar across ten inhabited bodies, and the family collecting on all of it carry the same word. Nobody in the breadbasket can name the sun that feeds them without naming the house that owns the shelf it sits on.

    Out on the moons the older common word for the sun is still in use in daily speech. It appears in no contract, no ledger and no filing, and three separate people told us the same thing about it: you do not use it in front of buyers.

    The Ministry of Propaganda INTACT

    That is its actual name, in its own paperwork, since incorporation. The Guard has never seen anything to apologise for in the word.

    It makes the educational material for member worlds, the morale material for the service, and the coverage of ceremonies, and then it puts all of it out.

    The catch

    It does not own the transmitters.

    The interstellar relay network was built by religious organisations to carry sermons. When central government collapsed they defended those towers, hard, and they still own every one of them. So the most powerful information organ in the galaxy buys airtime, by the hour, from eleven separate proprietors, at rates that vary by proprietor and by what is in the broadcast.

    Two of the eleven refuse whole categories of material outright, and the refusals are in the correspondence.

    Airtime is the Ministry's single largest expense: 61,440,800 credits last year.

    Guard flight formation, embarked. Twelve hulls establishment.

    Squadron records are filed to the standard of all Guard flight formations: establishment, hull state, flying hours, sortie returns, and personnel by name, service number, rate and medical category.

    Medical category is the relevant field for personnel administration and is updated on notification.     The personnel series INTACT

    Why this volume can tell you the colour of a soldier's visor.

    A Guard records depot was closed down and its paper duplicates were released for disposal as superseded administrative material. The Restoration collected them. It was lawful and it was almost certainly not intended.

    The Guard files its people in extraordinary detail: colouring, height, old injuries, what kit they were issued, which faith they wrote on the form at seventeen, who gets the money if they die. Most of what this volume knows about anyone currently serving comes out of that one shipment.

    It runs to a single date, which is the day the depot last bundled its paper, and stops.

    Planetary Defence Forces INTACT

    Local armed establishments retained by member worlds under their accession terms. Not part of the Guard and not commanded by it.

    Prevalence

    22 member worlds retain a Planetary Defence Force. In every case the retention is expressly reserved in the accession instrument, and in every case the instrument limits the force to territorial defence.

    Merger

    Where a Planetary Defence Force has been absorbed into the Guard, the absorption is recorded as a transfer of persons and not of the formation. Personnel enter as individuals at assessed rank. No absorbed formation retains its name, its colours, or its battle honours, and the Guard's own establishment returns record no formation older than the Guard.

    Prior service

    Service in a Planetary Defence Force before accession, including service in a conflict against a party that later acceded, does not appear in Guard personnel records. The record begins at contract.

    The quarantine authority INTACT

    Biosecurity authority of the Polaris system. Seated in Kelton City. Regulates movement of organic material between the ten inhabited bodies.

    Basis

    The system grows single crops at planetary scale. A blight established on Weton would not be contained on Weton. The authority exists to prevent that and has, on the record, prevented it: no system-wide crop failure appears in any return this archive holds.

    Powers

    Inspection, seizure, destruction, and the closure of movement between bodies. Closure requires no external approval and is not appealable. Movement of persons is subject to the same instrument as movement of material.

    Use

    Filed. Closures ordered GC 4442 to GC 4461: 61. Mean duration 9 days. Longest, 214 days, Dorrow to Kelton, in a year in which the Dorrow milling wage was in dispute.

    The authority's returns record the biological grounds for each closure. The Restoration has verified the grounds in every case it could check and could check 44 of the 61.

    The Restoration INTACT

    Us. The people who put this volume together.

    A civilian society with no charter, no powers, and no authority to make anybody do anything. Founded in GC 4443 by nineteen people who thought somebody ought to be collecting what was left.

    Four hundred and eleven registered volunteers, of whom perhaps sixty to eighty do anything in a given year. Eleven paid staff. Funded by subscriptions and two endowments.

    What we have

    1,411,206 catalogued pages. 88,400 more transcribed off damaged media. 4,206 recorded testimonies. Three rooms.

    What we do not have

    Access. Between GC 4443 and now we have made 219 written applications to institutions holding material. We have had 61 replies. Nine of those granted access to anything.

    We are not historians and we do not issue findings. We print what we have, we mark how we came by it, and we say plainly when we are guessing.

    The Royal Houses INTACT

    They started as metalworkers.

    A guild with trade secrets got rich, and then powerful, and then crowned. There is no divine right anywhere in the story and no conquest either. The progression is in the commercial record at every step: articles, apprentice indentures, oaths of secrecy about process, schedules of charges. You can watch a trade body turn into a landed interest turn into a monarchy by reading its invoices.

    The court still speaks foundry. Titles, ensigns, the ceremonial of investiture, all of it is forge language, and a good deal of it is applied to objects and acts that have nothing to do with metal any more.

    Two capitals

    Maldo works. Shayron is where the crown lives and where the ceremonies happen. Parliament, ministries, embassies and the High Council are all on Maldo, on purpose, so the beautiful one never has to host the galaxy.

    Names

    Given name, then Vot, then house and line. Royal blood is spread very thin across a very large number of houses, and it comes with a seat and a small maintenance and not much else. Half the galaxy can claim some.

    The war

    They stayed out of it. Their account is prudence, the neighbours use other words, and neither is a document. What is certain is that the Royal fleet and the Royal archive both came through intact, which is why this volume knows more about a Royal childhood than about most worlds.

    Money

    Taxes from their own systems, dues from protectorates, and royalties from arrangements with third parties. The largest of those is Astonia, and it pays them by the head.

    Royal Shayron Defence Force INTACT

    The Crown's own soldiers, and the other army in the room whenever the Guard is in it.

    Shayron keeps a real military. Not the ivory line on the approach to the castle, which is ceremony, but formations with ranks, postings, transports and a rank structure that runs its own way: first and second sergeants, a whole ladder of them, arranged to a logic that predates the Guard and has never been brought into line with it.

    How close they are to the Guard

    Close. They train together, exercise together, and lend each other people, in the ordinary manner of two militaries that have never fought each other and both benefit from the arrangement. A Royal officer on a Guard transport is unusual enough to be worth a second look and not unusual enough to be reported.

    The oath is recited rather than sworn, and every soldier in the force has it by heart:

    "I serve the people of Shayron and uphold the dignity of the"

    Names

    A Royal soldier working outside Shayron very often is not using the one on his file. This is normal, it is authorised, and everybody on both sides of the arrangement knows it, which does not stop it being awkward whenever somebody says it out loud.

    The people who check you in on the capital world, and the only officials on Shayron who look bored.

    The Trailblazers INTACT

    Soldiers from both sides of a war nobody won, building ports for worlds the shipping lanes forgot. Grey coveralls, orange trim, and a shovel on the badge.

    Who they are

    Veterans of the Autumnal party and of C.O.R.D., in proportions the body does not record because its founding instrument states that prior service is not a matter for enquiry. As far as we can tell that is actually observed.

    What they do

    The war cut the lanes and whole sectors went dark. The Guard holds a monopoly on the little that still moves. The Trailblazers reopen the routes, build the port where none survived, and run it under concession: fixed term, revenue split with the local council, paid for in land and housing.

    They are the only organised logistics network in the settled galaxy operating outside Guard control, and they got there by dealing with local councils rather than with the Guard at all.

    What it cost them

    The founding accounts are held. The body ran at a loss for eleven years and its people went unpaid for seven of them. The arrears schedule is filed. It was settled in full in GC 4443.

    No walls

    Every Trailblazer installation in the concession filings has no perimeter, no watchtower, no emplacement and no armed establishment. We checked this against the construction schedules, which list no such item, and against three informants, who confirmed it with some amusement.

    Standing

    They hold seats on local councils on at least four worlds, in every case by the council's own instrument and not by any treaty.

    The Astonian Annexation INTACT

    Transfer of Astonia from Royal protectorate to Guard territory, GC 4419. Effected by instrument, with a preceding action.

    Stated grounds

    Cartel control of the territorial administration, and a public health emergency. The emergency is documented: a wave of fatal overdoses across the principal cities over fourteen months, with a filed figure of 4,118 deaths, and one death of a prominent person which is the subject of most of the surviving ministerial material.

    Sequence, as filed

    Contested territorial election, GC 4417, with allegations of interference lodged by two parties. Formal warnings to the territorial administration, GC 4418, three in number, held here in full. Orbital interdiction and search and seizure operations, GC 4419. Instrument of annexation, same year.

    Effect on cartel revenue

    Filed and substantial. Prosecutions in the following three years: 2,411. Assets seized: 880,400,000 credits. The Restoration has verified the reduction in trade against the shipping returns and finds it real.

    The Royal position

    Astonia was a Royal protectorate. The houses did not contest the annexation. The instrument executed alongside it provides for a continuing royalty to the Royal houses on conscription yield, mineral rights and dairy export, in perpetuity, subject to accounting by the Guard.

    The accounting is performed by the Guard. The Royal treasury receives the figure and the payment. It does not receive the underlying returns and has not, on the record, requested them.

    Preceding documents

    Two Guard medical surveys of the Astonian population are dated GC 4416, being three years before the annexation and one year before the contested election. They are catalogued under Astonians.

    The Destruction of Wake CONTESTED

    The most talked-about event in living memory, and the one nobody can agree on.

    What the Guard says

    One ordnance deployment, Autumnal forces, GC 4394. Over in under an hour. Responsibility stated flatly, with no source cited and no unit named. It appears as settled fact in every piece of Guard educational material.

    What the people say

    We collected thirty-eight accounts across eleven settlements and six worlds, all of them from people who were children then or repeating a parent. Every single one describes something that took days. Two to nine of them. Six say the sky changed colour before anything was heard. Four describe evacuation orders. One describes those orders being cancelled.

    An hour and nine days are not two versions of one event.

    We note, and draw nothing from it, that the account was published by the party that later received the exclusive licence to mine the remains, and that there is nobody left on the other side to answer it.

    How many died

    Between 900 million and 4 billion. Neither number rests on a document. Both rest on people.

    The Great War CONTESTED

    also known as: the War · the Last War · the Long Account (Katanzaria)

    Two powers went to war and both of them ceased to exist. Nothing succeeded either one. Everything in this volume is dated from it and nobody can tell you why it started.

    When

    It stopped in GC 4402 and no source disputes that. It started somewhere between GC 4386 and GC 4393 depending on which world you ask, a spread of seven years. Some of that is worlds dating the war from the first fighting in their own sky. Not all of it is.

    Why

    Every world has an answer. No two answers agree. No document has been recovered that would let anyone prefer one.

    Our view, marked as inference and held loosely: this is not lost data. There was never one story to lose. INFERRED

    How it was fought

    Look at the requisitions and the damage assessments and the targets come up in the same order every time: shipyards, weapons manufacture, plasma extraction, medicine, banks. Ground taken and ground lost barely appear.

    They were not trying to hold each other's worlds. They were taking each other's capacity to make things, and they succeeded, and that is why a galaxy that can still fly cannot build a ship.

    Who was on which side

    We cannot draw the map. The best evidence is tax filings, because allegiance was decided by whom you paid, and they give roughly 65 worlds one way and 72 the other with everything else neutral, split, or paying both.

    Nineteen worlds appear in the collection records of both parties in the same year.

    The two atrocities

    The Wipe, laid at C.O.R.D.'s door. The destruction of Wake, laid at the Autumnals'. In both cases the accusation is made by the other side, and in one of those cases the other side is not there to answer it.

    [Compiler's note: we have been asked several times to produce a map. We have not produced a map.]

    The Kitalia Platform Collapse INFERRED

    Loss of one platform city, Kitalia, GC 4461. The structure entered the water. It was not recovered and has not been raised.

    The structure

    INTACT. Commissioned GC 4388. Foundation depth 1,610 metres across 214 pylons. Design load 4.1 million tonnes. Certified storm tolerance 260 knots sustained. Last full inspection GC 4459, passed without qualification. Construction cost 1,204,000,000 credits. Insured value at loss 1,411,000,000 credits, settled in full.

    Cause

    Charges at the pylon heads, placed by cells operating on the world. The Guard investigated, identified four cells, and cleared them out. What this archive holds is the summary; the working material behind it was never released, which is ordinary.

    The dead

    Not established. The platform roll was held on the platform.

    The Restoration's estimate is inferred from the structure and not from the population, there being no surviving record of the population. Taking certified residential floor area against the mean occupancy density returned for comparable platforms in the last decennial survey, the figure falls between 9,000 and 26,000 persons. We publish the method with the number because the number is a guess.

    There is no rubble field. There are no recovered remains. The register of missing persons compiled by the surviving platform administrations is open and is still receiving entries.

    [Compiler's note: we can tell you what the structure cost to the credit. We cannot tell you how many people were standing on it.]

    The Monver Refusal TESTIMONY

    The founding event of Monver. A colonial force refused an order to exterminate the population it had been sent to displace, and fought its own fleet.

    Date

    Approximately two thousand years before the present. No document survives from either party. The sending government has not existed for a comparable period and is not identified in any account we hold.

    Account

    Consistent across every Monveri source and not attested anywhere else. A colonial expedition established itself over decades, mingled with the native population, and received an order for their extermination. The expedition refused. The refusal became a guerrilla war against the fleet that had brought it, fought on the ground the expedition had settled, and won.

    Inheritance

    Every distinctive feature of Monveri political life is stated locally as descending from this event: the primacy of local government over distant authority, the refusal to impose on any other world's independence, and the fact that Monver has never founded a colony.

    Note

    Monver's accession instrument with the Guard provides two years of universal service in exchange for guarantees of non-interference in local government, statute and observance. Monveri sources describe the instrument as the same bargain their founders were given, drafted this time by the party that has to keep it.

    Attributed to eleven informants across four settlements.

    The Refugee Displacement INFERRED

    The largest movement of people that has ever happened, and the thinnest file in this archive.

    Somewhere between four and nine billion, by our own estimate, from housing stock, ration issues and port arrivals on forty-one worlds. Other figures in circulation run from two billion to eleven.

    Why it broke everything

    The receiving worlds could not manufacture. Housing, water, medicine and food could be moved and could not be made. A world of four hundred million taking in a billion people was not facing a policy question. It was facing arithmetic.

    What worlds did, from the port records
    • Took everyone, 9 worlds
    • Took them and camped them, 22 worlds
    • Took some, chosen against stated criteria, 31 worlds
    • Refused, 19 worlds
    • Refused, and fired on the ships, 6 worlds

    Each of those is a category of surviving document, because port authorities file their orders and the orders lasted.

    What it did to the map

    People moved along survival lines, not along which side they were on. So almost every world came out of it holding a population from the other side of the war, and the fighting inside borders started before anybody declared anything.

    And what everyone learned

    That where you were standing decided whether you lived. Which is why, when the Guard offered free movement between member worlds, that is the clause the accession debates argue about.

    Still unfinished

    Whether the descendants of those arrivals are citizens is a live question in the statute of forty-four worlds in this volume. In twelve of them it is unresolved in the third generation.

    [Compiler's note: this is the largest thing that ever happened to ordinary people in this galaxy, and it is four pages.]

    The Wipe INTACT

    vernacular: the Fry

    In GC 4401 every computer in the galaxy stopped, and everything any of them was holding stopped with it. Paper survived. That is the entire reason this volume exists.

    The formal word is the Wipe, and it is what the filings and the law use. Everybody who was actually there calls it the Fry.

    How complete

    Total, as far as anything we can check. In nineteen years nobody on any world has described to us a device that kept working, and no archive anywhere has reported a surviving data holding. We keep the request open.

    What went with it
    • every network. Communication fell back to couriers, unamplified radio, and towers the churches owned
    • every account. Money became paper, then became an entry in a Guard ledger
    • every drone and every unmanned system. Saigo is still trying to rebuild them
    • every navigational archive. The lanes were re-surveyed by hand over thirty years, and the survey authority publishes what that cost in ships and crews
    • the census

    What survived

    Insurers, port authorities, tax offices, monasteries and shipping clerks, all of whom kept duplicates in cabinets because that was the procedure. By weight this archive is about eighty per cent commercial and administrative paperwork.

    Which is why we can tell you the tonnage of a cargo that left a world sixty years ago and not how many people were living on it.

    [Compiler's note: the Guard's accounting division is understood to have retyped twenty years of ledger by hand after the event. We have applied four times to see it and have received three acknowledgements.]

    Rites

    33 entries
    Ancestor faiths TESTIMONY

    Talking to your own dead. It is the most common religious practice in the galaxy and almost nobody who does it calls it religion.

    It is not one faith. It is a shape that has appeared independently on more worlds than anything else in this volume, and the versions share nothing but the direction they face. A shelf in the corner with something on it. A word at a graveside. A place left at the table. Telling them about your day. On Nancast, small faceless iron figures kept in the house.

    What they believe

    Asked directly whether the dead can hear them, people answer that they can, that they cannot, and that it is not what the practice is for. All three answers come from people doing the identical thing.

    Nothing is written down

    No world files a return on what people do in their own kitchens, and no authority has ever had a reason to count it. This is the largest religion in the galaxy and it has no records at all.

    Aster TESTIMONY

    A goddess of the Shayron tradition, who is held to act sideways.

    The devotion is personal and domestic rather than congregational, and the phrase everyone uses is close to identical: Aster works in ways you are not meant to understand at the time. It is what people say when something has gone badly and they are not ready to call it meaningless.

    Whether she is her own figure or an aspect of Tracine is argued about by the people who observe her, and we are not qualified to settle it. Both accounts are held here.

    Cargo cults TESTIMONY

    The faiths that grew where the ships stopped coming.

    Why they are worse here

    The historical version of this happens to people who saw wealth arrive and then leave. What happened in GC 4401 was different in scale: populations that had instant medicine, interstellar travel and constant communication lost all three inside a day, and a good number of them lost every outside contact permanently.

    They are not imagining a golden age. They remember it. Some of them are old enough to have used it.

    What they do

    Keep the landing grounds clear, and nothing lands. Maintain dead machines with real care. Hold observances at the feet of relay towers that no longer speak. Set goods aside against a return. Treat any surviving pre-war object as sacred rather than merely valuable, which is a distinction that stops mattering after two generations.

    The characteristic object is a piece of pre-war manufacture, non-functional, whose purpose nobody alive knows, around which an entire account has grown up.

    One thing we will say plainly

    This archive has received two credible reports of communities holding ordnance in this way. We reported both. We were not told what happened next.

    The Collective TESTIMONY

    the faith has no name of its own. This heading is ours

    When you die your soul joins every other soul, and that accumulation is God.

    Not a god who was there first and made everything. God is what the dead have built, is still being built, and you are going to be part of it.

    Which makes being good urgent

    If people are cruel, God becomes cruel, and then everyone who dies afterwards goes into a cruel God. Adherents do not talk about this in terms of sin or reward. They talk about it the way an engineer talks about a structure that everybody is adding to whether they mean to or not.

    Praying means addressing the entire dead history of your own kind. Not asking. Contributing.

    Where you find it

    Scattered, unorganised, out on the cold moons, and among raider populations that will not accept contact of any other kind. Missionaries carried it from Sonaff. Versions of it turn up on inner worlds and we are not certain they are the same faith.

    A distinction

    The Maspin returning to the ocean under their crust is not this. They are describing something they consider a physical fact, not an afterlife.

    Custodial labour INTACT

    Prison work. Not a camp exactly, and not a prison exactly either.

    A sentence can be extended by administrative decision on grounds set out in a schedule. The grounds are broad, the decision is not appealable, and the numbers are unambiguous: 41,206 terms extended over twenty years, against 88 reduced.

    Where

    Two Guard installations take most of it. One of them mines magnetic ore. What that ore is for does not appear anywhere.

    Who

    The rolls are kept by species. Non-humans are about a fifth of everyone alive and about three fifths of these rolls. Targath turn up at a rate the population numbers cannot account for.

    Why it is defended

    Guard material puts it in terms of the bigger picture: the work needs doing, the sentences exist anyway, and member states that fall behind on their obligations can be reminded that both of those things are true.

    Dreamwalking TESTIMONY

    The belief that the soul is tied to the body rather than kept inside it, and that in deep sleep or unconsciousness the tie goes slack.

    While it is slack the soul can be moved. Including, adherents say, through time.

    The mechanics they describe

    Consciousness has something like weight, and that weight pulls it back toward its body. Overcome the pull and it goes elsewhere. A stretch of unconsciousness earlier in your life leaves the body unoccupied for that long, and that unoccupied time stays available afterwards. Two days in a coma at twenty buys you two days at forty, and while you are using them you are twenty.

    They also hold that this was once done with instruments rather than by accident, and that a device existed for pointing a soul somewhere rather than merely loosening it.

    Where it turns up

    Among Maspin practitioners working with floom preparations, in two monastic traditions on Shayron, and in the folk medicine of four worlds with no connection to each other.

    Why we have not dismissed it

    Religious testimony is normally consistent about meaning and wildly inconsistent about mechanism. This is the other way round. The accounts agree in detail about how it is supposed to work and disagree about what it is for, and we do not know what to make of that.

    The Elder Tree interment rite TESTIMONY

    How the Maspin bury their dead, which is not burial.

    The chamber fills. Somebody starts singing and the room takes it up. The person being interred walks to the edge of the opening in the floor and sings over it. Then the hood comes down, the necklace comes off and is set on the ground, and they step backward into the hole.

    Blue steam comes up afterwards and the tree takes it in.

    The stone from the necklace goes into the wall.

    Everyone attends

    Humans, Maspin, anybody who is there. Nothing is arranged differently for outsiders and nobody is warned in advance what they are about to watch. Two of the three visitors who described this to us had no idea what was happening until it had happened.

    They walk

    Every account has the person going to the edge unassisted and stepping back on their own. We asked, as plainly as we could manage, whether the timing is chosen by the person being interred. They understood the question perfectly well. They did not think it was an important one.

    Even graves grow flowers, I may sink like a stone, For what we know, for what we know, But you'll never be alone.

    The enlistment rites form INTACT

    Six questions you answer on your first day, about your own body.

    Burned or buried. Which faith, from a list of eighty-eight, with a blank line if yours is not on it. Whether your family wants you sent home at their own cost. Two names. Your signature. The date.

    You cannot start without filling it in, and once filed it is kept forever, because decades later it is the document somebody reads to find out what to do with you.

    It can be changed at any time by writing in. Fewer than two people in a hundred ever do.

    [Compiler's note: it is a good form. It is well drafted and it is honoured. The volunteer transcribing the GC 4444 series stopped for the day when she noticed what the ages in the third column were.]

    Foundation Day INTACT

    The Guard's birthday, and the best-documented event in this volume by an enormous margin.

    Same date every year since GC 4406. Assembly at nine, an address by whichever Director is nearest, a parade, a flyover if there is a fleet in the system, food for everybody, and a broadcast in the evening. It is not a religious holiday and the Guard is clear about that.

    It is also observed almost everywhere. Twelve member worlds hold it on a different local date, for harvest or weather reasons, each by a written dispensation, each of which we have.

    Why we hold so much of it

    Because the Guard photographed itself. We have the incorporation papers, the register of all fifty-six observances, the parade orders, the vendor licences, the road closures, the catering invoices, and 4,192 photographic plates.

    Attendance at the main event last year: 218,406, counted at the gate.

    [Compiler's note: this entry took an afternoon. The one after it in this volume took nine years and is four sentences long.]

    Galactic Standard law INTACT

    The code that runs everywhere, sitting on top of whatever your own world does.

    A member world writes its own statutes and the Guard leaves them alone. It can strike any of them at any time and in fifty-three years has done so forty-one times, thirty-eight of which were about tax or port dues, because that is what the Guard actually minds about.

    The part that matters

    The code applies everywhere. Enforcement does not, and nothing in the code requires it to. There is no provision for complaining that a law was applied to you and not your neighbour, and no body that would hear it.

    So automatic plasma weapons are lawful under local statute on nineteen worlds and unlawful under the code on all of them, and both facts sit there until somebody needs one of them. A world can run for decades doing something openly and then find out it was illegal the whole time, on the day that becomes useful.

    The laws are not there to be applied. They are there to be available.

    Slavery

    Prohibited absolutely, in the strongest language in the entire code. There is no inspectorate, no penalty schedule, and no enforcement mechanism attached to it.

    The gem-setting practice TESTIMONY

    Every Maspin wears a stone. When they die, it goes into the wall.

    It is taken off the necklace they wore in life and set by somebody from the household, or by a councillor, wherever there happens to be room. No inscription, no date, nothing written at all.

    Asked how a family finds their own stone afterwards, they said that they do not, and looked mildly puzzled that anyone would want to.

    The Gift of Memory TESTIMONY

    You do not tell a Maspin what happened to you. You give them a tear and they feel it.

    Do not tell. Share a tear.

    At the festival someone comes to collect it. You hold a memory, a real one, whatever moves you, and it goes into a single tear, and that is taken. Love, grief, joy, the worst thing you have ever seen. The kind does not matter.

    It has to be true

    A memory picked for effect is detectable, is an insult, and the Maspin will not explain how they know.

    What it is for

    It is how they come to understand another person. They do not assume understanding and they do not ask for it. It is given once, deliberately, and it costs the giver something to hand over.

    The Council asks for one from foreign parties. It sits in the minutes alongside credits and shipping like any other term of an agreement, because to the Maspin it is one.

    Several cultures in this volume forbid a person from ever speaking about certain things. When someone from one of those worlds gives this gift, they have not found a clever way around their own rule. They have broken it.

    Guard burial rites INTACT

    Whatever you wrote on the form when you signed, the Guard does. That is the promise and it is kept.

    Cremation or burial, your faith or none of them, a plot on the Burial Moon at no cost, your remains transported, and two family members brought out at the Guard's expense to stand there.

    Anything beyond that is chargeable: a custom stone, a particular plot, a third relative, or sending you home to your own world instead.

    When there are no remains

    The obligation is discharged with a service and no interment, and the name goes onto the memorial walls at the annual addition like everyone else.

    When there are too many

    One paragraph in the schedule permits a single combined service, at the caretakers' discretion, when the numbers are past what the moon can handle.

    It has been used.

    The Guard franchise INTACT

    Everybody votes, the votes are counted honestly, and the count is published. There is no fraud in this entry.

    Every Guard citizen of age gets one vote. Citizenship of your own planet gets you nothing here; you can hold local office on it and still not vote in a Guard poll. Registers are kept by the worlds and audited by the Guard, and fifty-three years of returns exist for every world and district, with the question printed in full.

    What gets voted on

    Over the last twenty years: 88 polls on roads and transit works, 61 on drug licensing, 44 on municipal boundaries, 39 on holidays and observance dates, 31 on harbour works, 22 on schools, and 106 on assorted local statute.

    What does not

    Appropriations. Licensing. Who sits on the Board. Standing orders. Whether an operation happens.

    Turnout averages 79.4 per cent and has been climbing for a decade. People vote because voting works. The things they vote on are the things nobody upstairs minds losing.

    Humanist supremacy TESTIMONY

    That humans are a superior order of thing, that spreading through the stars is theirs by right, and that whatever was done to get here needed no excuse.

    It is not a religion anyone joins

    There is no body, no clergy, no rite, no text, no register. There is nothing to sign.

    It is also the single most widely expressed belief in this volume. It turns up unprompted in testimony from every human world we have surveyed, almost always from people who would tell you flatly that they hold no religious position of any kind.

    How it sounds

    Recorded word for word, on worlds with no contact with one another: that we are a near-perfect design. That the stars were left for us. That whatever happened, it got us here.

    Nobody teaches it and nobody argues with it

    No institution in this archive professes it. No institution in this archive contradicts it. Guard educational material describes human achievement in terms we have difficulty telling apart from the doctrine, and files it under history.
